lessons.title: Practice Method Overloading
lessons.description: Java allows multiple methods with the same name if their parameter signatures differ. Implement two multiply methods: multiply(int a, int b) and multiply(double a, double b). The test checks that Solution.multiply(2.5, 2.0) is about 5.0; Solution.multiply(3, 4) equals 12.
learning_objectives: Harbor pickers recount crates before dawn, and overload methods with different parameter types in Java.

tests.name: test_overloaded_multiply
tests.test_code: if (Solution.multiply(3, 4) != 12) throw new AssertionError("int multiply"); if (Math.abs(Solution.multiply(2.5, 2.0) - 5.0) > 0.001) throw new AssertionError("double multiply");

source.name: Oracle Java Tutorials — Overloading Methods — 'methods within a class can have the same name if they have different parameter lists'

lessons.title: Practice Helper Methods Formatting
lessons.description: Break down problems into small private/public helper methods. Implement formatName(String firstName, String lastName) returning the last name, a comma and a space, then the first name. The test checks that Solution.formatName("Grace", "Hopper" equals "Hopper, Grace".
learning_objectives: Mesa pickers recount crates before dawn, and format strings with String.

tests.name: test_format_name
tests.test_code: if (!"Hopper, Grace".equals(Solution.formatName("Grace", "Hopper"))) throw new AssertionError("Expected Hopper, Grace");
